nodes.description: Immutable constant 'count' (4444) used as the modulus for winner index selection.
Immutable public 'owner' address, initialized from msg.sender at deployment and used as the access-control authority.
Public uint256 storage holding the pseudo-random seed produced by chooseWinners and consumed by winner.
Public function that computes a seed from block values, enforces owner-only access, and writes randomlyChosenNumber.
Public view function that derives a winning index from randomlyChosenNumber and the supplied index parameter.
msg.sender, attacker-controllable caller identity used for the owner check in chooseWinners.
block.timestamp, miner/validator-influenced value mixed into the seed hash in chooseWinners.
Weak randomness construction: keccak256 over block.timestamp, blockhash, block.coinbase, block.gaslimit and block.difficulty, all predictable or miner-controllable.
Caller-supplied 'index' argument of winner(), concatenated with the seed to derive a winner.
Local 'number' in chooseWinners holding the hash output before it is stored in state.
Local 'number' in winner holding the hash of seed and index before the modulo reduction.

edges.reason: owner state variable is initialized directly from msg.sender, binding the privileged role to the deployer's caller identity.
chooseWinners gates execution with require(msg.sender == owner), making the caller identity the access-control condition.
chooseWinners branches on require(randomlyChosenNumber == 0) before writing the seed.
block.timestamp is consumed inside chooseWinners as the seed source, creating a timestamp-dependency condition.
block.timestamp flows directly into the keccak256 seed computation, letting a miner bias the resulting randomness.
The hash computed by the unsafe seed-generation operation is assigned to the local variable 'number'.
Local 'number' is written into the randomlyChosenNumber state variable, persisting the manipulable seed.
winner requires randomlyChosenNumber != 0 and reads the stored seed as the hashing input.
randomlyChosenNumber is packed with the index and hashed into the local 'number' inside winner.
The index parameter is an input of winner and drives the derived winning number.
The index parameter is concatenated with the seed inside the keccak256 call that produces the local 'number'.
The constant count (4444) is used as the modulo divisor on the hash output, bounding the result to 0..4443.

normalization_plan.reason: index is only a transient argument of winner and carries no independent state; fold it into the winner function node.
local 'number' exists solely to hold the output of the weak keccak256 seed computation before it is stored.
local 'number' in winner is an intermediate hash value derived entirely within winner and has no standalone semantics.
